85c7db09d2.q: What percentage of good employee ideas does research show get withheld from managers?
85c7db09d2.a: In surveys of financial service institutions with about 3,000 responses to open-ended comments that were rated by senior executive teams for novelty, feasibility, and value, approximately 60 percent of the top 100 rated ideas were withheld and not told to the immediate boss. Additionally, general surveys show that about 80 percent of employees routinely withhold some of the ideas and feedback they have.

0c2d5de73b.q: Why might AI chatbots alone not solve psychological safety barriers to employee feedback?
0c2d5de73b.a: If employees do not feel psychologically safe having a conversation with their boss face to face, throwing an AI chatbot into the system is not necessarily going to help with that. There are two primary psychological mechanisms why someone would withhold feedback: lack of psychological safety and feelings of lack of utility or futility about speaking up, and AI chatbots do not inherently address these root causes.

dfca7bf105.q: How can organizations use AI to better translate employee feedback for executive action?
dfca7bf105.a: Theory suggests AI can help take basic ideas employees give through surveys, town halls and focus groups and translate them into the language executives use that meets their KPIs and strategic goals. Since employees on the front lines encounter problems but may not have access to strategic goals in the same way leaders do, there is a language translation needed from lower levels to higher levels. If employee ideas are linked back to what executives are already working on, they stand a much better chance for success.
